newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 19.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* United Parcel Service said it reached a tentative agreement with its Teamsters union to end a 15-day old Teamsters strike.
* Stocks recouped about half of Friday's sharp selloff, as the Dow Industrials rose 108.7 to 7803.36.
* Texaco agreed to buy Monterey Resources.
* Toyota aims to nearly double its operating profit in the next few years.
* Smith Barney is moving toward a settlement of a sexual discrimination lawsuit brought by 26 current and former female employees.
* Hewlett-Packard's quarterly profit fell below analysts' expectations amid higher-than-expected expenses.
* Microsoft's purchase of a minority stake in Apple is being reviewed by the Justice Department.
* A Philadelphia Stock Exchange search committee is expected to nominate former Pacific Exchange head Leopold Korins to lead the regional exchange.
* An antitobacco lawyer was sued by a client who charged that the attorney's work in negotiating the proposed tobacco settlement undercut her lawsuit about second-hand smoke.
* Some critics argue the proposed tobacco pact needs to raise cigarette prices by another $1.50 a pack.
* Mexico's economy grew at an 8.8 percent rate in the second quarter.
* Columbia/HCA was sued by two more public pension funds.
* Grand Union may get emergency help of $75 million from some lenders, including George Soros' investment firm.
